repair_design.principle: A self-declared owner_ref is no longer treated as proof of custody. Custody must be anchored to the resolver's OWN LIVE containers and re-derived at decision time.
repair_design.why_registry_is_not_an_anchor: HQ227 accepted law requires that replacing the caller-visible _registry leaves adjudication UNCHANGED because construction-time authority snapshots are pinned. Making registry identity load-bearing converted that accepted immunity into a hard refusal and broke test_hq227_exact_instance_registry_replacement_cannot_change_pinned_owner_snapshot. Because SEMANTIC MUTATION is FORBIDDEN, the registry anchor was removed and custody re-derivation was narrowed to relation semantic content only. This is a real constraint discovered by exact proof, not an assumption.

required_invariant: The positive owner decision must depend on a custody binding the admitted caller cannot manufacture by reflection, by reconstructing caller-visible state, by rebinding a reachable seam, or by setting an owner reference to the victim.
root_cause: Custody was proven only by (a) a self-declared owner_ref field and (b) a sealed tuple. Neither proves the state belongs to this resolver: any caller could rebuild the state type carrying another owner's material plus a chosen owner_ref, and rebind the lexical ledger cell so the victim maps to it. HQ232 named these as invariants W2 and W3.
why_not_fully_established: Every anchor is itself reachable and re-assignable by the same admitted caller, so a caller who replaces all live anchors and rebinds the ledger in one coordinated step still authenticates. See 03_REFLECTION_SURFACE_AUDIT.json and 06_FINAL_DISPOSITION.json.
